Pete — thanks for the summary and the doc. Quick recap and recommended approach from our side (we can deep-dive in the tech call):

1) Recommended primary pattern (server-to-server): service accounts + short-lived signed tokens
   - You keep a service account per Redwood "integration" in your infra.
   - Use a private-key JWT (RFC7523) signed by your key store (KMS/HSM). Redwood accepts JWT bearer assertions via our /auth/token endpoint and issues short-lived access tokens scoped to the requested model/route.
   - Benefits: no long-lived API keys, deterministic mapping to Elara IAM, easier revocation.

2) Fallback / dev flow: scoped API keys with rule-based rate limits for non-sensitive test environments (we advise rotation and limited scope).

3) Rotation & tooling: support both automatic rotation (Redwood-managed key rollover) and customer-managed keys (KMS-backed). Recommended cadence: rotate signing keys every 90 days and rotate tokens every 1 hour. We provide a rotation_playbook and SDK helpers to make this smooth.

4) Auditability: all auth events (token issuance, validation fail, key swap) are logged to the customer audit stream (push to your SIEM or S3), and retained per contract. SOC2 artifact: we can provide an event export and schema for your auditors.

5) SDK snippets: attached a short quickstart and a node snippet for exchanging a signed JWT for a short-lived access token and calling the embeddings endpoint. See redwood_service_account_snippet.js.

Next steps / ask:
- We'll share the quickstart + rotation playbook in a follow-up email (attached).
- Can we schedule a 45-min implementation deep-dive on Tue, Jun 1 at 10:00am PT? We'll include Avery (platform integrations) and Aditya (security).
- If legal wants a draft SOW or DocuSign link, point us to the procurement contact and budget window.

I'll also upload an internal canary rollout plan (small subset of API keys + routing to dedicated infra) after the call so you have a safe test path.

Best,
